title: The Coleridge-Taylor memorial concert, December 1919
summary: Briggs and Collier read the program of 'A Coterie of Friends' at Wigmore Hall, organised by Edmund Jenkins with Cook and Latimore; four Syncopated Orchestra members, including Briggs, played.

blocks.x: We are going to go back to London, briefly, to pick up a couple of things, we missed earlier, on the concert in London that Mr. Briggs wants
Briggs
tell us about.
This was a concert that was given in --
This was a concert given in honor of Coleridge-Taylor. It was called "A Coterie of Friends".
And this was at the time that you were in London, with the Southern Syncopated Orchestra?
Certainly. And the concert was on Sunday, December 7th, 1919, at 3:00 p.m., at the Whigmore Hall on Whigmore Street, West London.

I want to tell you a few words, about "A Coterie of Friends," which represented dignitaries from the British Empire, who had come to London, to be recompensed for their efforts to the Empire, during World War I.
It so happened, that these members were all dignitaries, very big persons, officials, of the Empire, all races of men.
Briggs 330
They were very surprised and humiliated by the bitter negligence of the official authorities towards them. Their reception was ice cold, as we'd say.
So, with the aid of Mr. Latimore, and Dad Cook--Will Marion Cook -- and the dignitaries, they formed "A Coterie of Friends," which represented a cultural society of brotherhood.
This concert was organized entirely by Mr. Edmund T. Jenkins who was the president of this society.
He was the son of Daniel Jenkins?
And he was the son of Daniel Jenkins, the organizer of the Jenkins Orphanage in Charleston, South Carolina.
They honored Coleridge-Taylor, and I'd like my friend Mr. Cartier to leave the program to you --
I have the xerox
Briggs 331

copy of the program, in front of me, and they were primarily the conversations with Coleridge-Taylor, and they were, "Symphonic Variations on an African Aire", a song, "Hiawatha's Vision," solos by W.A. Mikell, "Scenes from an Imaginary Ballet", "Concerto In G-Minor." The soloist was Winifred Small. "A Monologue; the Clown and Columbine," with violin-cello and piano accompaniment. Gwendolyn Coleridge-Taylor --
She was what, the pianist on the --
Yes, she was the pianist.
And then there was a "Folk Rhapsody", which was written by Edmund T. Jenkins. And then two songs by Coleridge-Taylor, "A Son of the Sea," and "Beat, Beat, Drums".
And concluded with, "The March Ethiopia, Saluting of Colors."
And the orchestra was conducted
Briggs 332
by Edmund Jenkins.
But we had four members of the Syncopated Orchestra which (Unintelligible).
Right. Well, the orchestra -- the members of the orchestra were drawn primarily from the Royal --
The Royal Academy.
The Royal Academy --
Conservatory.
Conservatory. But they did include four members of the Southern Syncopated Orchestra.
Mr. Salmavee, is it pronounced?
Salnave.
Salnave, S-a-l-n-a-v-e.
Mr. Rivera, the bass.
Mr. Rivera, the bass.
Mr. Withers.
Mr. Frank Withers, on trombone, and, of course, Mr. Arthur
Briggs
Briggs, on trumpet.
Thirty members.
Thirty members of the orchestra. And that concert, again, according to the program notes, was December 7th, 1919.
Yes.
